text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday:
- Zagrebacka Banka is to settle blocked forex accounts for up to 5,000 German marks.

- Commentary: Croatia is likely to take full control of Eastern Slavonia, the last Serb-held enclave, by June 15, 1997. All sides seem to agree that the U.N. mandate in the area should expire on April 15, 1997.
- Bakers and millers fail to comply with a government's decision to cut prices of flour and bread.
- The government drafted a $67.3 million programme aimed at preventing forest fires on the Croatian coastland, of which a World Bank loan would account for $42 million.
- Stock market: Prices of most issues are on the steady rise. Zagrebacka Banka last week up 12.2 percent, hotelier Jadranturist 30.4 percent.
- Confectioner Kras had 14.5 million kuna net profit in 1995 of which eight million is to be paid as dividend to share-holders.
- Results of the government's pro-natality programme: the number of families with three or four children is growing.
- Poll: Only one in five citizens of the Croatian capital is a small share-holder. But only one fourth knows about movements on the capital market.
- Croatian branch of Australia's Coca Cola Amatil, a licensed bottler of the popular drink, opened the second Coca Cola factory in Croatia.
- Hoteliers which used a loan from the State Investment Bank HBOR may have to pay more than their entire summer's earnings for the first instalment of the principle. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
